classification.difficultyReason: Select the familiar area formula or decompose the shape into a rectangle and semicircle, or a square minus a triangular notch. Read the equal-side and right-angle givens to infer the square; no unsignposted insight is required.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of each figure. Give exact answers and, where an answer involves $\pi$, also an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Trapezium parallel7/9cm bases and perpendicular height5cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Original given dimensions/marks only; no computed answers displayed.

spec.description: Rectangle height5cm width6cm capped by semicircle radius3cm; original centre/diameter and two lower rightangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Original given dimensions/marks only; no computed answers displayed.

answer.worked:
The rectangle has width 6 cm because 3 cm is the radius of the semicircle.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=6(5)+\frac12\pi(3)^2\\A&=(30+\tfrac92\pi)\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx44.14\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Square side4cm indicated by three equal ticks and bottomrightangles, triangular notch of depth2cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Original given dimensions/marks only; no computed answers displayed.

answer.worked:
The equal-marked sides make a 4 cm square. Subtract its triangular notch.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=4^2-\frac12(4)(2)\\A&=12\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
